what_happened: After handoff the ego braked hard for no clear reason (17 to 8 m/s) while its plan drifted left out of its lane, away from the recorded path. Car 1 overtook it on the left, and the ego's front-left corner hit car 1 as the ego edged into its lane.

On a straight multi-lane highway, the policy took over at 4.6s, braked hard (17 to 8 m/s) for no clear reason, and steered left toward the next lane. The ego's front then hit the rear-right of actor 1, which was just ahead in that lane, while the recorded human path kept going straight in the original lane. The rear contact came later, probably caused by the sudden braking.

After handoff on a straight multi-lane highway, the policy braked hard for no visible reason (17 to 8 m/s, with the lead car pulling away) and steered left into the next lane. Its front hit vehicle 1, which was driving alongside in that left lane. The hard braking probably also explains the later rear contact.

Once the policy took over at 4.6 s on the highway, it braked hard for no clear reason (17 down to 9 m/s, while the lead car 18 was about 20 m ahead and pulling away) and drifted left into the next lane. Its front hit actor 1, which was driving alongside in that lane. The hard braking probably also caused the later rear-end hit.

After the policy took over at 4.6 s, its planned path (orange) bent left, and the ego drifted left out of the lane the recorded drive used. The ego braked hard for no clear reason, dropping from 20 to 11.6 m/s, and its side hit actor 1, a car moving alongside in the lane to its left, at 6.1 s. The rear contact recorded for this run came after this side collision.

Despite the RIGHT command, the ego stayed in its lane instead of moving right as the human did, running about 6–7 m off the recorded path. Actor 33, in the lane to its right and probably replaying the recording, moved left into the space the ego occupied and the two collided at 11.7 s (logged as a front collision) while the ego only slowed gently.

On a multi-lane highway with the command STRAIGHT and then RIGHT, the policy's planned path bent left, and the ego drifted into the lane on its left. There it hit actor 41, which was travelling alongside it on the left. The camera showed nothing broken before the impact, and the car ahead stayed 17 m or more away, so this was not a following-distance problem.

On a multi-lane highway with a STRAIGHT command (it changed to RIGHT at the end), the policy's planned path bent left toward the next lane while the recorded path went straight. The ego drifted left at about 4.5 m/s and its front-left hit actor 41, which was driving alongside in the left lane.

On a multi-lane highway with the command switching to RIGHT, the ego went the other way: its predicted path (orange) bent left and the ego drifted about 1.3 m left of the recorded trajectory, toward the next lane over. Actor 41 was coming up in that lane from behind on the left, and the ego's front-left hit it as it pulled alongside at 7.2 s.

The ego was creeping forward in slow, queued traffic and drifted right toward the lane line, about 2.8 m off the human path. At about 0.4 m/s its front-right corner clipped car 21, which sat ahead and to the right, just over the lane line. Car 24, directly ahead in the ego's lane, was still about 4.6 m away, so the ego did not hit the car it was following.

On a multi-lane highway with a STRAIGHT command, the policy's planned path (orange) veered left away from the recorded lane-keeping path (green). The ego drifted into the left adjacent lane and its front struck vehicle 41, which was travelling alongside on the left.

The ego was crawling forward in queued traffic on a STRAIGHT command, but it had drifted about 2.9 m left of the recorded path and was straddling the lane line. Its front-left corner crept into the rear of car 24, which was stopped in the adjacent left lane, at about 0.2 m/s. The gap to the car directly ahead was still about 4.6 m, so this was a lateral drift into the next lane's queue, not a failure to brake for its own lead.

The ego was going straight in a slow queue toward a red light and decelerated from 2.1 to 0.2 m/s, but it never fully stopped. It crept into the rear of the queued vehicle ahead in its lane (actor 24), causing a low-speed front collision about 2.9 m off the recorded path.

The road curves right and the command is RIGHT, but the policy kept a nearly straight heading at about 16–20 m/s. The ego drifted left across the yellow centerline and onto the left shoulder by the guardrail at 10.0s. There was no lead vehicle or other actor involved, and the camera view stayed coherent enough before the departure.

The ego was going straight in slow, queued traffic toward a red light. It slowed from 2.5 to 0.2 m/s but never fully stopped, and it crept into the rear of stopped lead vehicle 24, registering a low-speed front collision at 9.5 s. It was also drifting slightly right, about 2.8 m off the recorded path.

Going straight in slow, queued traffic, the ego drifted right of its lane center, ending up about 2.8 m from the recorded path and straddling the right lane line. It slowed from 2.8 to 0.4 m/s but never fully stopped, and at 9.0 s it crept into the front of the stopped car ahead (most likely actor 24, the closest car ahead), with a reported gap of about 4.6 m. A gap that size usually means no contact, so it may be measured between vehicle centers, and the overhead map doesn't clearly show which car was hit. The camera smearing is mostly on the bus and the cars right next to the ego and gets worse near impact, so it doesn't clearly explain the slow drift and late braking.

In stopped traffic, the ego crept forward about 2.9 m to the side of the recorded path, straddling the lane line between stopped car 24 ahead-left and car 21 ahead-right. It slowed to 0.2 m/s but never fully stopped, and its front corner touched the rear of car 24, which was stationary.

While creeping to a stop in a queue behind vehicle 24, the ego drifted about 2.9 m right of the recorded path, onto the lane line. At about 0.2 m/s its front right corner clipped vehicle 23, which was stopped or parked in the right lane next to it. The car ahead was still 4.6 m away, so this was not a rear-end of the lead vehicle.

The route command was RIGHT and the planned path curved right, but the ego stayed on the far left of the road, riding the yellow edge line, and slowed from 16.6 to 14.3 m/s. An actor had already hit its rear by then. At 11.7 s it had crossed the yellow line onto the left shoulder, which counts as offroad, just as actor 51 came alongside on the right and overlapped it, a contact not counted as the ego's fault.

Even with a RIGHT command, the ego drove about 1.5 m left of the recorded path, along the yellow centre line, and kept drifting left until it left the drivable area at 11.6 s, slowing from 15.6 to 13.5 m/s. An actor hit its rear sometime before 9.6 s, and actor 91 makes front contact right beside it at the end, but neither explains the leftward drift, which was already underway at 9.6 s.

On a gently curving road with a RIGHT command, the policy held a straight path (orange) while slowing from about 19 to 15 m/s, instead of following the green route as it bends right. The ego drifted left across the yellow centerline toward the left shoulder and guardrail, and went off the road at 10.2s, about 1.6 m from the recorded human path. No other actor was involved, and the camera view stayed coherent enough beforehand that rendering doesn't explain the drift.

The ego was going about 15 m/s on a curving divided highway with a RIGHT command, and its route bent right. Its plan instead pulled left, across the yellow left edge line and onto the left shoulder next to the guardrail, where offroad was flagged at 11.2 s. There was no actor ahead. The camera view is mostly intact, and actor 91 only comes up behind the ego at the very end, so the policy itself drove off the road.

The route command was RIGHT and the planned path curved right toward the lanes on the right. Instead, the ego held a slightly leftward heading along the yellow left edge line, slowing from 16.5 to 14.4 m/s, and drifted over it onto the left shoulder by the guardrail, ending 1.6 m off the human trajectory. No actor was close ahead, and the camera view, though smeared at the edges, showed the edge line and lanes clearly enough, so this was the policy's own lane-keeping error.
